question: What age group does the WHO classification typically cover for adolescents?
explanation: The World Health Organization defines adolescents as individuals between the ages of 10 and 19. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h1)

question: Why do traditional adult health clinics often fail young people?

options.A: They are always located outside major cities
options.B: They feel intimidating and judgmental to teenagers
options.C: They lack any qualified medical personnel
options.D: They only open during school hours exclusively

explanation: Young clients frequently avoid standard adult clinics because the environment feels unwelcoming and judgmental regarding sensitive health topics. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h1)

question: Which principle ensures that clinic opening times fit school schedules?
explanation: Accessibility involves logistical and temporal adjustments, making sure clinic hours do not clash with school or vocational training. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: What does acceptability mean in the context of youth-friendly clinics?

options.A: Staff maintain non-judgmental attitudes and respect client privacy
options.B: Only peer educators are allowed to dispense medications
options.C: Treatments are completely free of charge for everyone
options.D: Facilities must be built using modern architectural designs

explanation: Acceptability refers to the social and cultural comfort of the facility, heavily driven by respectful, non-judgmental staff interactions. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: A common nutritional deficiency observed among adolescent girls in Nigeria is:
explanation: Iron-deficiency anemia is highly prevalent among adolescent females due to menstrual blood loss and inadequate dietary intake. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: Why are mental health issues in teenagers frequently missed by adults?

options.A: Symptoms are often mistaken for normal teenage rebellion
options.B: Adolescents lack the capacity to experience depression
options.C: Hormonal changes make clinical diagnosis completely impossible
options.D: Standard psychiatric tests only work on adults over forty

explanation: Adults tend to normalize behavioral shifts as typical teenage moodiness, failing to recognize underlying clinical depression or anxiety. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is a major psychological barrier preventing youths from visiting clinics?

options.B: Fear of stigmatization by healthcare workers
options.D: Overly crowded waiting room television sets

explanation: Many young people avoid seeking help because they anticipate harsh moral judgments and scolding from healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h4)

question: How do strict parental consent policies negatively impact adolescent health?

options.A: They force parents to pay double for medical consultations
options.B: They delay the immunization schedules of newborn infants
options.C: They deter minors from seeking confidential care for sensitive issues
options.D: They eliminate the need for any physical examinations

explanation: Requiring parental approval for every service stops teenagers from visiting clinics for fear their parents will discover private matters. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h4)

question: What is the primary cornerstone for building trust with an adolescent client?
explanation: Adolescents require an assurance of privacy before they feel secure enough to share honest health histories. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: When is it legally and ethically necessary to breach adolescent confidentiality?

options.A: Whenever the parents demand to see the clinic records
options.B: If the teenager refuses to pay the consultation fee
options.C: As soon as a minor turns fifteen years of age
options.D: When the client expresses active suicidal ideation or abuse

explanation: Client safety always supersedes privacy limits when there is immediate danger of self-harm, suicide, or severe abuse. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h5)

question: An essential community outreach task for a nurse in AYFHS is:

options.A: Collecting local taxes from adolescent business owners
options.B: Organizing health talks in schools and youth centers
options.C: Issuing driver licenses to teenagers turning eighteen
options.D: Performing major surgeries in village market squares

explanation: Nurses extend care beyond hospital walls by conducting educational outreach sessions in places where young people gather. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h6)

question: Why do nurses train peer educators as part of youth health programs?

options.A: To replace professional nurses completely during night shifts
options.B: To enforce strict hospital rules on incoming patients
options.C: To reduce the overall budget allocated for medical equipment
options.D: To reach marginalized youths more effectively through trusted peers

explanation: Peer educators bridge cultural and age gaps, helping to disseminate accurate health information to groups who might distrust formal health workers. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h6)
